Fix maximizing i, define g=sgn K_i and f(x)=x_i g(x_without_i)-g(o_without_i); its edge oscillations are bounded by 2 and its i-edge oscillation attains 2, while the projected i-derivative at basepoint has modulus E|K_i|. This gives exact sharpness for arbitrary family and both real/complex scalars. Pointed translations U_y f(x)=f(xy)-f(y) diagonalize Walsh basis; averaging arbitrary projection onto the given span yields unique diagonal Q_A with norm not greater, and dual argument gives free-space minimality. For degree k shadows are degree k-1 Krawtchouk kernels; elementary symmetric walk identity gives quadratic coefficient m*binom(m-1,floor((m-1)/2))/2^{m-1}. Independent exact integer-Walsh checks exhausted all nonempty support families n=1,2,3 (1+7+127) and matched extrema. General proof, not finite testing, covers all n.
